author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand and his wife Laura get into one of the most unexpectedly funny conversations about Catholic hymns, debating which ones sound completely made up on the spot and which ones are genuinely beautiful. Russell argues that some hymns feel like whoever wrote them was trying to squeeze too many words into not enough melody, Laura defends her favourites, and they end up competing to find the best one before landing on The Lord Bless You and Keep You as the undisputed winner and the song that gave Russell actual goosebumps at school.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand and Alex Jones get into one of the most unexpectedly funny and deeply sincere conversations about prayer. Alex Jones reveals he is constantly in a state of prayer throughout the day, not always verbally but always spiritually connected, and that getting on your knees in private is something he considers absolutely key to his faith. Russell naturally takes it somewhere completely chaotic from there. Funny, genuine and surprisingly moving.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand reacts to footage of Britain's first South Asian councillor and mayor celebrating his position in overtly religious terms and asks the question that nobody in mainstream media will ask. Is this natural organic representation or does it have the feeling of a forced cultural agenda being pushed from above? Russell makes clear he has no issue with diversity in itself but argues that when change feels imposed rather than organic it creates exactly the kind of tension and resentment that serves the interests of those who want to keep ordinary people divided and distracted from the real sources of power.
